questions.stem: Which of the following is a principal organ of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The six principal organs are the General Assembly, the Security Council, ECOSOC, the International Court of Justice, the Secretariat and the Trusteeship Council. The Security Council has primary responsibility for international peace and security. A national legislature, a political party and a pre-colonial Yoruba council are not UN organs.

distractorRationale.a: The National Assembly is Nigeria's federal legislature
distractorRationale.c: The APC is a Nigerian political party of the Fourth Republic
distractorRationale.d: The Oyo Mesi was the council of state in the Oyo Empire

questions.stem: The veto in the United Nations Security Council is enjoyed by

options.text: all 193 member states of the General Assembly
the five permanent members of the Security Council

questions.explanation: China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States — the P5 — can each block a substantive Security Council resolution by a negative vote. That is the veto. The General Assembly has no veto; the Secretary-General does not; AU membership confers none.

distractorRationale.a: The General Assembly operates on a one-state-one-vote rule without a P5-style veto
distractorRationale.c: The Secretary-General heads the Secretariat and has no veto
distractorRationale.d: AU membership is unrelated to the UN veto

sources.title: Charter of the United Nations, Articles 23 and 27

questions.stem: The Organisation of African Unity was transformed into the African Union in
questions.explanation: The OAU was founded on 25 May 1963 in Addis Ababa. The AU was launched on 9 July 2002 in Durban, South Africa, after the Constitutive Act of 2000. 1975 is ECOWAS at Lagos; 1999 is the start of Nigeria's Fourth Republic (and the Sirte Declaration that proposed the AU, which is not the launch itself).

distractorRationale.a: 1963 is the founding of the OAU, not its replacement by the AU
distractorRationale.b: 1975 is the Treaty of Lagos that created ECOWAS
distractorRationale.d: 1999 is Nigeria's return to civilian rule; the Sirte Declaration that year proposed an AU but did not launch it

questions.stem: A feature of the African Union that distinguished it from the old OAU is

options.text: a complete ban on any discussion of human rights
provision for intervention in a member state in cases of war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity
the replacement of all African states by a single continental parliament with exclusive sovereignty
the abolition of heads of state

questions.explanation: The OAU treated non-interference as nearly sacred. The AU Constitutive Act allows the Union to intervene in respect of war crimes, genocide and crimes against humanity, and it adds democracy and integration to the older unity-and-liberation agenda. That is the contrast examiners want. The AU has not abolished states or heads of state.

distractorRationale.a: The AU emphasises human rights more, not less, than the OAU
distractorRationale.c: The AU is a union of sovereign states, not a single continental government
distractorRationale.d: The Assembly of Heads of State remains the AU's supreme organ

questions.stem: ECOWAS was established in 1975 by the
questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States was created by the Treaty of Lagos on 28 May 1975. The treaty was later revised in Abuja in 1993. Its aims are economic integration, free movement and, increasingly, regional peace. Versailles (1919), the UN Charter (1945) and Lyttleton (1954) are different documents.

distractorRationale.a: Versailles ended the First World War in 1919
distractorRationale.c: The UN Charter created the United Nations, not ECOWAS
distractorRationale.d: Lyttleton 1954 was a Nigerian colonial constitution

questions.stem: Nigeria hosts the ECOWAS Commission in Abuja and provided the bulk of troops and finance for ECOMOG operations in Liberia and Sierra Leone.
questions.explanation: True. Those two facts are the standard summary of Nigeria's role: institutional host and leading peacekeeper. They follow from Nigeria's size, oil revenue and Afrocentric foreign policy. Examiners treat them as required knowledge, not optional colour.

distractorRationale.b: Denying either the Abuja headquarters or the ECOMOG lead role contradicts the historical record taught on the WAEC syllabus
